transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I just barely sleep right anymore. I'll lie there in bed, and... I don't know, if I hear rain or start thinking about the bluff giving way, I just can't settle down. Then when I finally do pass out, I wake up all sweaty from these dreams. I end up showing up to my shift at the call center feeling like I never slept at all. It's just really wearing me down.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried most days, even when you're not trying to sleep?

Yeah, I do. Most days I just feel... scared, honestly. And embarrassed, kind of right under the surface all the time. It's like I walk around feeling like everyone can tell that I messed up, and... I don't know, like they can see I'm not as tough as I used to act.
Do you find yourself worrying about a lot of different things — like work, relationships, or everyday responsibilities — even when there isn't a clear reason to?

Not really, no. I mean, work is just work, you know? I just answer the phones. And I don't really stress about everyday stuff or relationships or anything like that. It's mostly just... what I said before. The rain, and thinking about the bluff. That's what I'm scared of, not really normal everyday things.

Have you ever had an episode where your heart started racing, you felt short of breath, or like you were having a hard time catching your breath, especially when it came out of nowhere and wasn't tied to a specific situation?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I mean, my heart might beat fast if I'm having one of those dreams or thinking about the bluff, but... it doesn't just happen out of nowhere. And I've never had a time where I couldn't catch my breath or anything.

Have you been having these dreams or thoughts about the bluff often? Like, do they come up during the day when you're not trying to sleep, or do you find yourself thinking about it even when you don't want to?

Yeah, they do. It's not just the dreams. Sometimes, I'll just be at work, and... stuff pops in my head out of nowhere. Like, I'll just suddenly hear the sound of rocks sliding, or I'll feel like my leg is stuck under me again. Just for a minute, it feels like I'm right back on that trail, instead of just sitting at my desk with my headset on. It just happens, even when I'm trying not to think about it.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of the bluff or what happened there?

Yeah, I do. I won't go anywhere near the coast trails now. And... I've been dodging texts from my hiking buddies lately, too. Just, even talking about going out there makes my chest tighten up, so it's easier to just not deal with it.
Have you noticed yourself being more on edge or easily startled since what happened on the bluff? Like, do you get irritable, have trouble focusing, or feel like you're always on high alert?

Yeah, definitely. I'm... I'm just a lot more on edge. Like, at work, my patience is just way shorter than it used to be. I've actually snapped at a few customers over really small stuff. It got bad enough the other day that I raised my voice, and my supervisor had to pull me aside to talk to me about it. I just... I get irritated so fast now.
